name: Contact, Unclassified
flavorText: It does not hunt and it does not posture. It walks a straight line toward something it has apparently already decided belongs to it, and removes what is in the way. The classification code is assigned afterward, in the debrief — during the fight nobody knows what to call it, which is the point.

immunities.name: all damage
immunities.duration: while the Interdiction Field is intact — see abilities

abilities.name: Interdiction Field
abilities.description: The Claimant is immune to all damage. The field has one weak point, which is not visible from Frame height — only from ground level, looking up. Breaking it is not a Frame-scale action at all: it is resolved by the ground team's Spot checks (see challenge day-1-ground-layer, Field Integrity pool, 6 points). When the pool is filled, the field collapses: the Claimant is Stunned 2 and gains weakness 15 to all damage for the rest of the encounter. Weakness 15 is the maximum level-appropriate value for level 12 (reference/tables/dc-and-check-math.json).

abilities.name: Scale-Blind
abilities.description: The Claimant cannot perceive creatures of Medium size or smaller, and its Strikes can only target Large or larger creatures and objects. It threatens ground-level characters only through Advance's collateral hazards. This is the Scale Disparity rule from design/scale-and-chassis.md §8, written into the statblock rather than applied as a GM ruling — and it is the in-fiction reason the ground team can work directly beneath it.

abilities.name: Advance
abilities.description: The Claimant moves up to its Speed toward its objective, ignoring difficult terrain and destroying any structure smaller than itself in its path. Each time it Advances, one collateral hazard triggers at ground level (challenge day-1-ground-layer). It uses this every round it is not Stunned; it does not pursue, retreat, or change target. It is not fighting the Frame — the Frame is in the way.

abilities.name: Claim
abilities.description: Trigger: a creature or object of Large or larger size ends its movement adjacent to the Claimant. Effect: the Claimant makes a Sweep Strike against it. This is why standing in front of it works as a delaying tactic and also why it hurts.

notes:
Day 1's Claimant, for episode-01-contact-unclassified scene 7. Built from the GM Core creature-building tables at level 12: AC High (33), Fort High (+25), Ref Low (+19), Will Moderate (+22), Perception High (+25), Strike attack Moderate (+24), Strike damage Moderate (3d8+12). HP is deliberately Low for its level (165, band 165-157) rather than High: its real defence is the Interdiction Field, and the fight is scripted for the Frame to win, so the HP number's job is to decide HOW LONG the berserk rampage lasts, not whether the Frame survives. Attack and damage are Moderate rather than High for the same reason — it is not trying to kill the Frame, it is trying to get past it, which is both the lore ('a property dispute humanity is losing') and the thing that keeps a scripted first fight from accidentally killing the party's only launched Frame. Not yet named or numbered: it is classified as Claimant One in scene 9's debrief, which is what the episode title refers to.

speed.land and Sweep's reach trait were rescaled 10x on 2026-08-22 (40->400, reach-30->reach-300) alongside every other distance in design/scale-and-chassis.md's battlefield — a reskin of the same numbers onto 50ft squares, not a redesign; see design/scale-and-chassis.md §14f.
